_comment: Example global memory grant. Copy to $COFFERDAM_HOME/config/mind-grant.json and
edit on the workstation — this file is an example and is never read by the
service.
THIS FILE IS THE GRANT. Without it, Cofferdam has no global mind at all: not a
refused one, an absent one. Nothing scans your home directory, your Documents
folder or an existing Obsidian vault, nothing offers a directory it found, and
Cofferdam never chooses where your vault lives. You write the path down once,
here, on the machine.
There is no API route that creates, edits or reads this file. A grant that could
be written over the network would be access that could be granted over the
network — the same reason there is no create route for a project.
'root' must be a plain absolute path — no ~, no $VAR, no '..'. It is verified
again immediately before every read and every apply: each component is checked
for a symlink, the resolved path must equal the configured one, and it must be a
readable directory. A vault reached through a link is refused. Keep it OUTSIDE
$COFFERDAM_HOME: the vault is yours, and Cofferdam does not own it.
'documents' maps a code-owned ROLE to a file inside the vault. The global roles
are user, communication_style and preferences. An unmapped role has no file at
all — Cofferdam never guesses a filename, even an obvious one sitting right
there — and a role named twice is refused rather than resolved by position.
'enabled': false turns the grant off without deleting it. Deleting the file is
the complete revocation.
The vault is plain Markdown in an ordinary directory: Obsidian-compatible, and
Obsidian-independent. Cofferdam never launches Obsidian, never reads .obsidian/
and never writes its configuration. Your vault works in a text editor with
Cofferdam stopped.
Reading is local. Nothing in this milestone sends memory to a model, a cloud
worker, the private Custom GPT or a browser.
See docs/MIND.md.
